definitions.explanation: A person who gathers at the scene of an accident, fire, or other incident out of curiosity rather than involvement. Carries a negative nuance of being nosy or getting in the way.

examples.japanese: {野次馬|やじうま}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{集|あつ}まった→集まる：01162_atsumaru⟧。
⟦{事故|じこ}→事故：00851_jiko⟧⟦{現場|げんば}→現場：02723_genba⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{野次馬|やじうま}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大勢|おおぜい}→大勢：02850_oozei⟧⟦{集|あつ}まっていた→集まる：01162_atsumaru⟧。
examples.english: A large crowd of onlookers had gathered at the accident scene.

examples.japanese: {野次馬|やじうま}⟦{根性|こんじょう}→根性：19215_konjou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{見|み}→見る：00283_miru⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧はやめ⟦なさい→なさる：01307_nasaru⟧。
examples.english: Stop going to look out of idle curiosity.

notes:
USAGE:
{野次馬|やじうま} is almost always negative, implying nosiness or interference. It describes people who crowd around incidents without any real connection to what happened.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {野次馬|やじうま}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{集|あつ}まる→集まる：01162_atsumaru⟧ (onlookers gather)
- {野次馬|やじうま}⟦{根性|こんじょう}→根性：19215_konjou⟧ (idle curiosity; rubbernecking mentality)
- {野次馬|やじうま}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{追|お}い{払|はら}う→追い払う：06347_oiharau⟧ (to shoo away onlookers)

ETYMOLOGY:
Originally referred to an old, useless horse ({親父馬|おやじうま}) that was unruly and hard to control, later applied to noisy, meddlesome spectators.
